records.issue_text: isAccessTokenId matcher reads wrong substring index: grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6) but code uses substring(3, 5), reading the last char of token type plus first char of grant
records.rationale: The access token ID format is defined in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` as 6 chars before `:`: `sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grantShort(2) + ':' + rawId`. Therefore the 2-char grant shortcut occupies indices `[4,6)` (0-based), matching the provider’s own parsing in `getTokenContextFromTokenId(...)` (`gtShortcut = encodedContext.substring(4, 6)`). However `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)` uses `items[0].substring(3, 5)`, which reads one char from the tokenType and one from the grant shortcut, so it will mis-validate token IDs.
records.stripped_text: isAccessTokenId matcher reads wrong substring index: grant shortcut is at substring(4, 6) but code uses substring(3, 5), reading the last char of token type plus first char of grant

records.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `rawTokenId` is not actually null-checked due to a copy/paste error: the 4th check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`. This allows `rawTokenId` to be null without failing fast, matching the finding.
